hero.lead: A nation of 18.3 million from the Galapagos to the Amazon, backed by a $5 billion IMF programme and $1.55 billion of new World Bank finance in 2026.

capital.heading: Ecuador is financing reform and local infrastructure at once. Next, every child reading by ten.

register.name: International bonds 2034 and 2039
register.detail: Issued January 2026 · average interest rate 8.98% · $3 billion used to buy back earlier bonds
register.note: Net $1 billion for fiscal financing
register.text: Ecuador’s return to the international bond market, with new bonds maturing in 2034 and 2039. Three-quarters of the proceeds bought back earlier bonds, and the rest financed the budget that carries the seven standards.

register.name: Amazon Biocorridor debt conversion
register.detail: Announced 17 December 2024 · $1 billion of DFC political risk insurance · IDB liquidity guarantee
register.note: About $1.53 billion of international bonds refinanced
register.text: A debt conversion that refinanced international bonds and is expected to generate about $460 million for Amazon conservation over 17 years. It aims to improve the management of 4.6 million hectares of protected areas and protect 1.8 million more hectares of forests and wetlands, the source of the water and livelihoods of the Amazon.

register.name: Galapagos debt-for-nature swap
register.detail: 11 May 2023 · $656 million blue loan · $656 million of DFC political risk insurance · $85 million IDB guarantee
register.note: Global bonds of 2030, 2035 and 2040 exchanged
register.text: Ecuador exchanged about $1.63 billion of global bonds for a $656 million blue loan, freeing more than $18 million a year for 18.5 years for marine conservation in the Galapagos through the Galapagos Life Fund. Healthy fisheries sustain food and livelihood on the islands.

register.name: Subnational infrastructure finance
register.detail: Approved 24 September 2026 · Multiphase programme, three phases over ten years · first phase $200 million
register.note: Through Banco de Desarrollo del Ecuador; $50 million of parallel cofinancing from AECID
register.text: A ten-year programme that finances energy, transport and sustainable mobility, urban development, disaster-risk management and affordable housing for local governments. Local roads, power and homes carry the shelter and energy standards to towns that national budgets reach last.

register.name: Reforms for investment and jobs
register.detail: Approved July 2026 · Budget support
register.note: IBRD loan
register.text: Makes public spending more efficient, improves social transfers and manages fiscal risks.

register.name: Fiscal and jobs programme with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option
register.detail: Approved 26 November 2025 · $900 million programme · $200 million Cat DDO
register.note: Two operations in one package
register.text: Budget support for sound fiscal management, private-sector growth and jobs while protecting the most vulnerable, and a contingent credit line for climate, geophysical and public health risks. It keeps health and livelihood financed when a shock strikes.

register.name: Social Safety Net, additional financing
register.detail: 11 February 2025 · includes a $10 million grant from the Global Concessional Financing Facility
register.note: Cash transfers for the first 1,000 days of life
register.text: Cash transfers, conditional on health and child development services, for poor households with young children, with an updated Social Registry. It aims to reduce chronic child malnutrition, for the food and health standards.

register.name: Mangroves for Climate (FP235)
register.detail: Approved 18 July 2024 · grant · under implementation to 2030
register.note: About 30% disbursed
register.text: Restores and manages mangroves on Ecuador’s coast with local communities and shrimp farms, with results-based payments to end deforestation. Mangroves protect the fisheries and livelihoods of the coast.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility
register.detail: Approved May 2024, augmented July 2025 · Fifth review 22 April 2026
register.note: About $3.7 billion disbursed; about $394 million released in April 2026
register.text: Growth of 2.5 percent is projected for 2026.

register.name: IDB CLIMA National Water Security Program
register.detail: Approved 21 October 2026 · $124.76 million IDB and GCF loans · $3.72 million GCF grant
register.note: Green lending through Banco de Desarrollo del Ecuador
register.text: A programme to improve water security for the population groups it targets, by expanding the green lending of the Development Bank of Ecuador. It is aimed at the water standard.

register.name: Program to Strengthen Macroeconomic Stabilization
register.detail: Approved 2 September 2026 · Special Development Lending, multi-tranche
register.note: Budget support
register.text: Budget support to reinforce fiscal sustainability and stability in monetary markets. A stable budget keeps the public services behind the seven standards funded.

register.name: Financing Low-Income Housing in Ecuador II
register.detail: Approved 10 December 2025 · partial credit guarantee
register.note: Affordable mortgages through financial intermediaries
register.text: A guarantee that expands affordable mortgage credit for middle-income households, to reduce the housing deficit. It is aimed at the shelter standard.

register.name: Institution-Strengthening Program to Prevent and Respond to Violence and Crime (IS-PREVIC)
register.detail: Approved 25 June 2025 · policy-based loan · closed
register.note: Budget support
register.text: A policy-based loan to strengthen the State’s capacity to reduce criminal violence and illicit financial flows. Safety is the condition for a livelihood.

register.name: Caja Central Financoop, bond for women-led microenterprises
register.detail: 29 September 2026 · bond of up to $20 million
register.note: IDB Invest share; the rest from other investors
register.text: Financing for microenterprises owned or led by women, lent through the savings and credit cooperatives affiliated with Financoop. It is aimed at the livelihood standard.

register.name: Banco Internacional, syndicated loan for small and medium enterprises
register.detail: 24 September 2026 · IDB Invest up to $50 million · JICA TADAC fund up to $25 million
register.note: With technical assistance to digitise SME lending
register.text: A syndicated loan of up to $100 million that widens credit for small and medium enterprises. It is aimed at the livelihood standard.

register.name: Villonaco III wind farm
register.detail: Approved 2026 · loan · not yet signed · about 112 MW in Loja
register.note: Sponsor: Cobra Group
register.text: A loan for a wind farm of about 112 MW in the province of Loja, developed by Villonacoenergy. New wind power adds to the renewable electricity that already carries most of the grid, for the energy standard.

register.name: Produbanco, subordinated loan
register.detail: 29 April 2026 · $20 million disbursed
register.note: Small businesses, including those of older adults
register.text: A subordinated loan that strengthens Produbanco’s capital so that it can lend more to small and medium enterprises, and to agriculture, construction, water efficiency and energy projects. It is aimed at the livelihood standard.

register.name: Banco Bolivariano biodiversity bond
register.detail: 6 March 2026 · IDB Invest $50 million · IFC $50 million · FMO $20 million
register.note: Ecuador’s first biodiversity bond
register.text: A bond whose proceeds finance projects under Banco Bolivariano’s Biodiversity Financing Framework. It puts private credit behind the land and water that sustain livelihoods.

register.name: Banco Pichincha, subordinated loan
register.detail: 20 January 2025 · IFC $55 million · $45 million mobilised
register.note: Women-led microenterprises and climate-resilient farming and fishing
register.text: A subordinated loan that expands lending to women-led microenterprises and to sustainable, climate-resilient agriculture and fishing. It is aimed at the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: Produbanco, loan for biodiversity and women-owned firms
register.detail: 29 October 2024 · loan of up to $100 million
register.note: The first loan in Ecuador with a component earmarked for biodiversity
register.text: A loan for projects that conserve and restore biodiversity, climate-smart projects and credit for women-owned small and medium enterprises. It is aimed at the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 63 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A market in an Andean town in Ecuador

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Banana plantations in the coastal lowlands of Ecuador

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Cloud forest in the Andes of Ecuador, mist among the trees

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: A river in the Ecuadorian Amazon

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of electricity from renewables, 2023
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: A hydropower dam in the Andes of Ecuador

items.name: Omarsa
items.text: One of Ecuador’s two largest shrimp exporters, farming, processing and exporting shrimp since 1977; IFC lent up to $20 million in 2023 for a new 536-hectare farm in Guayas.

items.name: Interagua
items.text: The private company that runs water and sanitation for Guayaquil under a 30-year concession, financed to raise water and wastewater coverage to 95% of the population by 2031.

items.name: Compañía de Titularización Hipotecaria (CTH)
items.text: Buys home mortgages from lenders and sells them as securities on Ecuador’s stock market, widening finance for housing.

items.name: Universidad de Las Américas (UDLA)
items.text: A private university in Quito with about 15,700 students, financed to build a new campus for up to 2,000 more.

items.name: Grupo Conclina
items.text: Ecuador’s leading health services group and owner of the Hospital Metropolitano, the largest private hospital in the country; IFC lent $25 million in 2024 for a new hospital in Cumbayá.

items.name: Caja Central Financoop
items.text: A cooperative second-tier lender with 27 years of experience, financing women-led microenterprises through savings and credit cooperatives across Ecuador.
